passages.title: Meeting Isla at last
passages.text: Four years ago, my English teacher organised an online exchange with a school in Edinburgh. Every student in our class was given a partner to write to, and mine was a girl (1) ______ name was Isla. At first I was not very keen (2) ______ the idea, because I have never enjoyed writing long messages. But the emails from Isla were so funny that I always replied straight away. Soon we were chatting by video every weekend, (3) ______ though we had never met. Last July my parents finally agreed to take me to Scotland. On the train I felt nervous, and (4) ______ worried me most was that we would have nothing to say to each other face to face. In fact, (5) ______ was no reason to worry at all. Isla was waiting on the platform holding a big sign with my name on it, and we started talking at once. I stayed with her family for a week and even had a little room of my (6) ______ at the top of the house. Now we are planning her visit to my town next spring.

questions.question: Write ONE word that fits gap (1).
questions.explanation: Whose is the possessive relative pronoun: "a girl whose name was Isla" means a girl, and her name was Isla. Who or that cannot be followed directly by a noun like name.

questions.question: Write ONE word that fits gap (2).
questions.explanation: The fixed phrase is keen on something: "I was not very keen on the idea". No other preposition is used after keen with a noun.

questions.question: Write ONE word that fits gap (3).
questions.explanation: Even though introduces a surprising contrast: they chatted every weekend "even though we had never met". Only even fits before though in one word here.

questions.question: Write ONE word that fits gap (4).
questions.explanation: What means the thing that and starts the subject of the clause: "and what worried me most was that we would have nothing to say". No other single word can start this clause.

questions.question: Write ONE word that fits gap (5).
questions.explanation: There was introduces something that exists (or here, does not exist): "there was no reason to worry at all". It was no reason is not correct English.

questions.question: Write ONE word that fits gap (6).
questions.explanation: The fixed pattern is a + noun + of + my own: "had a little room of my own", meaning a room only for the writer. No other word fits after of my.
